The M30 Luftwaffe Drilling was a bizarre 3-barreled survival weapon designed for German WWII pilots — combining two 12-gauge shotgun barrels with a rifle barrel underneath, all in one exquisitely crafted firearm. Only around 2,500 were ever produced, and surviving examples now sell at auction for tens of thousands of dollars. Watch the full story of this rare WWII combination gun at Simple History.

The M3 Grease Gun packed a hidden magazine loader right into its wire buttstock. This WWII submachine gun replaced the pricier Thompson and used this simple loading tab to make reloading 45 ACP magazines faster and less painful. Discover this clever piece of WWII weapon engineering and more hidden firearm features at Simple History.
